thread:
maria (sec): Heads up — we're rolling out a new org-wide policy: all long-lived API keys will be deprecated in favor of short-lived tokens (OIDC/Client Credentials) with a max TTL of 24h. This starts next week and affects hosted API keys, service keys, and personal dev tokens.

ben (platform): TL;DR: long-lived keys older than 90 days will be revoked on 2026-05-15T00:00:00Z. Migrations should be done before that.

priya (sdk): What does this mean for SDK workflows and local dev?

maria (sec): Good question — for dev: use the new 'rw auth login' which exchanges SSO for a short-lived CLI token. SDKs will automatically refresh when using the client-credentials flow (docs linked below). We'll publish migration guides.

jamie (infra-oncall): Action items for infra teams: 1) find and list any long-lived keys used by automation/cron jobs; 2) switch to workload-identity or OIDC where possible; 3) update CI secrets to use ephemeral tokens via the new tokenbroker.

alex (eng): Any grace periods or exemptions for partner integrations?

maria (sec): Exemptions are limited. If a third-party cannot support short-lived tokens, open a request in #eng-security with the owner and justification. Exemptions auto-expire after 30 days and require a mitigation plan.

ben (platform): Quick commands: to find long-lived keys in the console run:
```
# list API keys older than 90d
redwood-admin keys list --older-than 90d --format json | jq '.[] | {id: .id, owner: .owner, created: .created_at}'
```
If you need bulk rotation we can run a one-time job — ping me.

priya (sdk): Docs link?

security-bot: Automated notice: New Policy "API_KEYS_SHORT_TTL" published: https://internal.redwood/sec/policies/api-keys-short-ttl. Effective date: 2026-05-01.

maria (sec): Migration checklist (short):
- inventory keys (console/CI/repos)
- update CI to use tokenbroker (example in docs)
- replace service account keys with OIDC or client-credentials
- rotate any key used for scheduled jobs to short-lived tokens
- verify no hard-coded keys in repos (see grep snippet below)

ben (platform): Repo scan snippet:
```
grep -R "redwood_api_key" --exclude-dir={.git,node_modules} || true
```
If you find matches, tag the repo and create a remediation PR.

jamie (infra-oncall): If a runbook needs updating, please add a short note under /runbooks/auth. We'll mark critical runbooks for review.

alex (eng): Who will revoke remaining old keys?

maria (sec): On 2026-05-15 at 00:00 UTC we will automatically revoke keys flagged in the 90d bucket. We will send a 48-hour and 2-hour warning to owners via email and Slack DMs. If revocation breaks something, open an incident in #eng-oncall and we'll temporarily re-enable a single key for investigation.

priya (sdk): Does this change token format or scopes?

ben (platform): Token format remains JWT-ish, but we've added audience claims and more granular scopes (read:embedding, write:deploy). Update your token validators — there will be a small compatibility shim for 30 days.

maria (sec): Security reasons: long-lived keys are the single biggest contributor to stolen-credential incidents we see. Moving to short-lived tokens reduces blast radius and makes key compromise window much smaller.

alex (eng): Any immediate steps I should do today?

maria (sec): Yes — run the inventory command, search repos, and open tickets for any automation that can't use OIDC. Tag me or ben if you need priority help.

security-bot: Reminder scheduled: Inventory report due by 2026-05-01 12:00 UTC. Use `/security inventory report --team <team>` to submit.

ben (platform): We'll be holding two office hours next Tue/Wed 1600 UTC to help teams migrate. Booking link in the policy doc.

jamie (infra-oncall): FYI — infra will temporarily whitelist tokenbroker IPs for CI runners during migration window.

maria (sec): Thanks all. I know this is a bit of work up front, but it will cut down on incidents and help us meet enterprise security requirements. Please escalate blockers early. :lock: :rocket:
